confirmed.what_breaks: The order view's delegated click listener calls ACTIONS[button.dataset.action] for every button carrying data-action. A banner shown in the page region of the order view (APP-01 from the window error listener, STO-05 from a blocked save) carries a Reload button with data-action='reload', which ACTIONS does not know, so the click throws a TypeError; the window error listener then shows a second APP-01 banner before the body listener reloads the page. The reload still happens, so the user sees only a replaced banner for an instant.
confirmed.evidence: main.js:45 and :50 give STO-05 and APP-01 the action { label: 'Reload', name: 'reload' }; components.js:43 builds it with actionButton(label, 'link', spec.action.name), which sets data-action='reload' at :14. main.js:145 puts a banner in the first [data-banner-region] of the document; index.html:12-18 has none in the header, so on the order view that region is pageBanner (order-view.js:211, appended inside root at :358). A click on Reload reaches the root listener at order-view.js:345-348 before the body listener: closest('button[data-action]') finds the button, it is not disabled, ACTIONS['reload'] is undefined, so the call at :348 throws TypeError. The error reaches the window 'error' listener (main.js:292), which shows APP-01 in the same region, then the body listener (main.js:289-291) calls location.reload(). blocked.js:58-61, customer-detail.js:167-168 and customer-list.js:131-132 compare the action name first and cannot throw. Advisory: the page reloads as the button promises; only the banner flashes.

confirmed.what_breaks: F-35 (accepted in cycle 2) asked every view to take the shape render(container, viewModel, actions) of ADR-003 with one delegated listener per container. Two views still take the whole context with the mutable state: customer-detail.js reads state and commit from it, and order-list.js reads state, writes state.searchOrders itself and keeps a listener on the search input and on a Clear search button that is rebuilt on every search. The S12 and S13 fix commits say F-35 is fixed, so the accepted finding is half closed.
confirmed.evidence: ADR-003, Decision: 'A view has the shape render(container, viewModel, actions) and one delegated listener per container (JS-11)'. customer-detail.js:131 'export function renderCustomerDetail(container, context)', :132 destructures route, state, commit, openDialog, showBanner, deps, locale from it, :133 and :151 read state.data. order-list.js:134 'export function renderOrderList(container, context)', :135 reads context.state, :120 and :126 write state.searchOrders, :125 input.addEventListener('input', ...), :77 empty.querySelector('button').addEventListener('click', onClear) on a button that resultsPanel rebuilds at :117 on every keystroke, the case JS-11 names. main.js:72 maps customer: renderCustomerDetail and orders: renderOrderList straight to the context call at main.js:237, while the five other screens go through wrappers at main.js:75-97 that build a view model and actions. The diff of c9cc2ba (S12) changed customer-detail.js to one click listener and kept the context signature; no commit in scope touches order-list.js for F-35 (271ba2d changed only the locale line).

confirmed.what_breaks: Two new shape tests carry requirement ids that name a form rule the test contradicts or does not cover: the title at :140 is tagged R-11 and asserts that the stored shape accepts a quantity of 0, while R-11 says a quantity is a whole number from 1 to 9 999; the title at :149 is tagged R-15 for the same storage rule. The rule both tests prove is ADR-004's 'form rules are not checked' (R-20), so a trace of R-11 or R-15 lands on tests that say the opposite of the requirement. The commit-message half of the finding is not raised: the human rejected F-41 ('a commit message is history, not rewritten').
confirmed.evidence: shape.test.js:140 'R-11 hasValidShape accepts a line with unit price 0 and a line with quantity 0', :144-146 set quantity = 0 and assert hasValidShape true. REQUIREMENTS.md R-11: 'a quantity that is a whole number from 1 to 9 999'. shape.test.js:149 'R-15 hasValidShape accepts an order whose total is exactly Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER' tests shape.js:38-40, a storage check. shape.test.js:175 names the rule these tests belong to: 'because form rules are not checked' (R-20). PLAN.md:178 S7 '**Covers:** R-06, R-19, R-20, R-21, R-32' lists neither R-11 nor R-15. TS-02: a test 'is named after the requirement id and that behaviour'. The gate's trace step passes because R-11 and R-15 are also named in money.test.js, validation.test.js and lines.test.js.

confirmed.what_breaks: The test title promises invisible characters 'on either side of the @', but all four cases put them before the @, and the hasText(parts[1]) term it would cover is dead code: whenever parts[1] contains the dot the next term requires, the dot (category Po) already keeps INVISIBLE_ONLY from matching, so hasText(parts[1]) is always true. The test proves only the left side and the code carries a check that changes no behaviour.
confirmed.evidence: validation.test.js:206 cases are U+200B@b.c, U+FE0F@b.c, U+034F U+200B@b.c and ' U+200B@b.c', every invisible run before the @. validation.js:51-52: valid = parts.length === 2 && hasText(parts[0]) && hasText(parts[1]) && parts[1].includes('.'); INVISIBLE_ONLY = /^[\p{Cf}\p{Z}\p{Mn}\s]*$/u cannot match a string holding '.', so hasText(parts[1]) is true whenever includes('.') is true, and when includes('.') is false the conjunction is false whatever hasText says. The mutation run proves it: the planted defect validation.js:52 '1' -> '2' that turns hasText(parts[1]) into hasText(parts[2]) (= !INVISIBLE_ONLY.test(undefined) = !test('undefined') = true for every input) survived with every test green, while the sibling mutant on parts[1].includes was caught by the TypeError it throws. The term is therefore redundant and untested, as the finder says. Advisory: no input is accepted or refused differently.

confirmed.what_breaks: The title of the id test still says the id rule refuses 'characters outside a-z, 0-9, - and _', while the code and the new test in this scope accept uppercase letters. The title describes a narrower rule than the one enforced and tested, so a reader of the test list learns the wrong rule.
confirmed.evidence: shape.test.js:108 'R-20 hasValidShape refuses an empty id, the id new and an id with characters outside a-z, 0-9, - and _'. shape.js:4 'const ID_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/;'. shape.test.js:167-171 'R-20 hasValidShape accepts ids with uppercase letters and refuses a plus sign' sets id 'Bob1_Z-A' and asserts hasValidShape true. Both tests pass in this run (node --test tests/shape.test.js: 24 pass), so the two titles describe two different rules for one pattern.

watchList.what_breaks: INVISIBLE_ONLY now covers the whole Unicode class Mn (nonspacing marks). That is wider than R-17's 'zero-width or other format characters': a required field made only of combining marks that render on a dotted circle (U+0301, a Thai vowel mark) is refused as empty, although R-01 counts it as 1 character. Same root cause as CON-4.
watchList.evidence: validation.js:7 INVISIBLE_ONLY = /^[\p{Cf}\p{Z}\p{Mn}\s]*$/u; :43 refuses any text it matches when min > 0. For name U+0301: textOf (:34) keeps it (trim removes only whitespace), INVISIBLE_ONLY.test is true because U+0301 is Mn, so validateCustomer returns customer.name.length. The F-13 fix (accepted) wanted U+FE0F and U+034F refused, both Mn; the human did not say whether every Mn character counts as invisible. REQUIREMENTS.md R-17: 'zero-width or other format characters'.
watchList.why_unproven: Whether a field made only of combining marks is 'invisible' under R-17 or a valid 1-character name under R-01 is a reading of the requirement, not a fact the code settles.
watchList.how_to_settle: The human says whether a required field made only of combining marks counts as empty. If yes, R-17 is amended to say so and validation.test.js adds U+0301 as refused; if no, S2 replaces \p{Mn} with the explicit zero-width marks (U+034F, U+FE00 to U+FE0F, U+180B to U+180D) and adds U+0301 as accepted.

watchList.what_breaks: The empty-text check includes the whole class Mn, which also holds visible combining accents, so a required field made only of such marks is refused as empty and R-17 may not mean that. Same root cause as COR-4; one answer settles both.
watchList.evidence: REQUIREMENTS.md R-17: 'A text made only of invisible characters (zero-width or other format characters) counts as empty for every required field'. validation.js:7 'const INVISIBLE_ONLY = /^[\p{Cf}\p{Z}\p{Mn}\s]*$/u;'. The new tests at validation.test.js:186-190 and :199-203 feed only U+FE0F and U+034F, which are zero-width.
watchList.why_unproven: Two readings of R-17 both hold on its text: only zero-width and format characters, or anything with no standalone glyph. The human has decided the delete case of F-13 only, not the breadth of the class.
watchList.how_to_settle: Same question as COR-4: the human says whether a field made only of combining accents counts as empty; the fix follows that answer in S2.

watchList.what_breaks: A customer name or line description made only of blank letters or symbols that are not format, separator or nonspacing-mark characters (U+3164 HANGUL FILLER, U+FFA0, U+115F, U+2800 BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK) still counts as text, so a customer or line is saved whose name shows as a blank row link in the list, the picker and the order list.
watchList.evidence: validation.js:7 INVISIBLE_ONLY = /^[\p{Cf}\p{Z}\p{Mn}\s]*$/u; U+3164 is general category Lo and U+2800 is So, neither in the class. For name U+3164: textOf (:34) keeps it, INVISIBLE_ONLY.test is false, length 1 is within 1 to 100 (:44), so validateCustomer returns ok and the name is stored; validateLine (:112) takes the same path for a description. R-17 names 'zero-width or other format characters' only; cycle 2 F-13 left U+3164, U+2800 and U+0001 as 'a separate question for the human', and the archived decisions carry no answer.
watchList.why_unproven: The behaviour is proven, but R-17's letter does not cover these characters, so whether anything breaks depends on a requirement the human has not written.
watchList.how_to_settle: The human says whether blank-rendering letters and symbols count as empty under R-17. If yes, R-17 names them, S2 adds an explicit list to INVISIBLE_ONLY and validation.test.js feeds U+3164 and U+2800 as refused; if no, the finding is closed as the letter of R-17.

watchList.what_breaks: After a customer's name or email is corrected, the text typed to find them stays in the Search customers or Search orders box; only a new customer or a delete clears a search. The box can show the old spelling with 'No customers match this search.' until the user types or reloads.
watchList.evidence: Rule LD-04: 'Personal data can be corrected, and the correction reaches every place it is shown'. main.js:124 clears state.searchCustomers only when state.route.name is 'customer-new' or customerWasDeleted(nextData); :125 clears state.searchOrders only on customerWasDeleted; no branch covers 'customer-edit'. Path: type 'Jane Smiht' in Search customers, open her, correct the name to 'Jane Smith', save (commit at customer-form.js:114 lands on the detail), go back to Customers: customer-list.js:95 sets input.value = searchText = 'Jane Smiht' and searchCustomers finds nothing. ADR-005 (accepted): the search texts 'survive moving between screens and are gone after a reload'. The accepted F-43 treated the same text as a copy of the person's data for the delete case (LD-07). The archived cycle 2 decisions hold no answer for the carried LEG-10.
watchList.why_unproven: Whether a search box holds the user's query (ADR-005) or a copy of personal data (the F-43 reading) for a correction is a reading the human made for deletes only; the record itself is shown corrected everywhere it is displayed.
watchList.how_to_settle: The human says whether the F-43 reading extends to a correction. If yes, commit clears both search texts when state.route.name is 'customer-edit' and MANUAL-CHECKS.md gets the R-02 line; if no, ADR-005 stands and the finding is closed.

equivalent.why: compareById runs only when compareNames gave 0, and ids are unique (shape.js:81 refuses duplicate customer ids on load, deps.newId is crypto.randomUUID), so a.id === b.id never holds for two distinct customers and < and <= answer the same; Array.prototype.sort reads only the sign.
-1 became -2: Array.prototype.sort reads only the sign of the comparator, so every order it produces is unchanged.
With unique ids the two operands are never equal, so > and >= give the same answer for every pair the sort passes.
-1 became -2: Array.prototype.sort reads only the sign of the comparator, so every order it produces is unchanged.
The 0 branch is reached only when a.id === b.id, which unique ids rule out for two distinct customers; the sort never compares an element with itself, so the value is never returned.

sumIsExact only tests Number.isSafeInteger(sum); subtracting every line total from 0 gives the exact negation of the sum, isSafeInteger is symmetric in sign, and lineTotalCents still throws on an unsafe product, so the answer is identical for every input.
The line runs only inside if (a.date !== b.date), so the two date strings are never equal and < and <= give the same answer.

The surviving mutant is hasText(parts[1]) -> hasText(parts[2]) (the sibling on parts[1].includes throws a TypeError and was caught). hasText(parts[2]) is !INVISIBLE_ONLY.test(undefined) = !test('undefined') = true, and the original hasText(parts[1]) is also true whenever parts[1].includes('.') holds, because '.' is category Po and outside the class; when includes('.') is false both versions are false. The term is dead code, which is COR-3.

hasSafeTotal only tests Number.isSafeInteger of the reduce result; subtracting every line total from 0 gives the exact negation and isSafeInteger is symmetric in sign, so the answer is identical for every input.

The fallback is returned only when ORDER_NUMBER does not match. hasCanonicalNumber (:49) then compares order.number with 'ORD-' plus the padded value, which a string that failed /^ORD-(\d{4,})$/ can never equal whatever the value, so it stays false; hasValidLinks (:86) runs only after data.orders.every(isOrder) passed (:103-104), when every number matches, so the fallback never decides the result.
